instagram_caption:
A $36 billion fund made $160 billion of bets. Then it broke in less than a week.

Archegos Capital, run by Bill Hwang, eventually managed about $36 billion, but borrowing took its exposure to stocks to about $160 billion, about $4.40 for every $1. In late March 2021 those stocks fell, lenders demanded cash, and Archegos couldn't pay. More than $100 billion of market value in its stocks was wiped out in days. Banks lost more than $10 billion; Credit Suisse alone lost $5.5 billion. Hwang was convicted of fraud in July 2024 and sentenced to 18 years in prison.

Did you know a fund could borrow that much?

Sources: NBC News, AP, US DOJ SDNY (2024). Not financial advice.
